author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved in collaborative session 2026-05-12.

DECISION RECORD

D1 (Wire format): Path B with empty array fallback. Add a separate Message.broadcastMentions: BroadcastMention[] array, always present (defaults to []). User mentions stay in Message.mentions (per-user, unchanged structure). BroadcastMention object has fields {scope: "everyone" | "here" | "admins", offset: UnsignedInt, length: UnsignedInt}. Rationale: structural separation between user-mention-by-id and broadcast-by-scope-predicate; matches the semantic distinction even at the cost of an additional always-present empty array.

D2 (Rich-body span): D2-A. One new span type 'broadcast' with fields {type: "broadcast", scope: "everyone" | "here" | "admins", text: <String>}. Existing 'mention' span stays user-only (carries userId). Companion: line 1257 of main draft updated to 'Both `mentions` and `broadcastMentions` arrays on the Message MUST be empty; all mention information (user and broadcast) is carried inline within the spans.'

D3 (Permission model): Umbrella, renamed. Single permission gates all broadcast scopes. Replace the existing 'mention_all' permission name at main draft :584 with 'mention_broadcast' (the old name referred to the dropped '@all' synonym and no longer reflects what the permission gates). Deployments that want granular per-scope authorization layer it on top via deployment-specific policy per 38055ec.

D4a (Predicate definition): Impl-defined. Spec the semantic intent only:
- @everyone targets all current members of the Space/Chat (deterministic)
- @here targets active members; the exact predicate (which presence states qualify) is deployment-defined
- @admins targets members with administrative authority; the exact predicate (which permissions/roles count, whether controller principals from §Space Governance are included) is deployment-defined
Consistent with c93e545/2fd3cf7/38055ec impl-defined-authorization pattern.

D4b (Resolution timing): Hybrid. Send-time set is INFORMATIONAL — the sending server MAY compute and ship a resolved id list (for sender-side UX: 'you @here'd these N people'). Delivery-time check on each receiving server is AUTHORITATIVE for push urgency, badging, and notification routing. Each receiving server evaluates its own predicate at delivery time against its local presence/role view. Matches the receiver-side-authoritative pattern (membership, blocked-sender, receiveTypingIndicators are all delivery-time checks).

D5 (Suppression preferences): D5-Impl. Default behavior: broadcast mentions to targeted recipients bypass Chat.muted (and any active Chat.muteUntil period) for elevated urgency. Opt-out is deployment-defined; no new wire field added. Spec text should clarify this in main draft Chat.muted definition (line 445 area) and add an explicit security/UX note. Privacy-conscious deployments can ship per-user 'always honor mute' controls without touching wire format.

D5-sub (Per-scope opt-out): Future bead. No major chat product ships per-scope mute granularity at the spec level; YAGNI. The D5 wire contract is forward-compatible — per-scope opt-out can be added later via new Boolean fields or via the existing impl-defined opt-out channel.

D6 (Push payload): D6-Typed. Replace hasMentionAll with mentionScopes: String[] (array of "everyone" | "here" | "admins" values present in the message). hasMention remains for user mentions, computed per the existing ex4u/f86f4f4 rule (Message.mentions OR rich-body 'mention' span). The mentionScopes field computes analogously: Message.broadcastMentions UNION rich-body 'broadcast' spans, mapped to scope strings. Empty array means no broadcast scopes; non-empty means at least one. mentionUrgency triggers if mentionScopes is non-empty OR hasMention is true (replacing the current 'hasMention || hasMentionAll' check).

M1 (Staging): All three scopes ship together in one spec rev. No production deployments at draft-00 to validate staging against; doing it once is simpler.

M2 + 6gzj.4 (Naming): Canonical textual form is '@everyone'. Wire enum value 'everyone' already locked at D1. Textual aliases ('@all', etc.) are deployment-side UI policy, not wire contract.

DOWNSTREAM IMPLEMENTATION SCOPE

fig9.2 (main draft):
- Replace Mention's bead-implied per-user-only definition with the wire spec above (add broadcastMentions field on Message; add BroadcastMention object; add 'broadcast' rich-body span; update line 1257 rich-body emptiness rule)
- Rename mention_all permission to mention_broadcast at line 584 and throughout
- Add spec text for @here / @admins predicate (impl-defined) and resolution timing (hybrid)
- Add Chat.muted bypass clarification for targeted-recipient broadcast mentions
- Add Security Considerations note about broadcast-mention abuse vectors and the deployment-defined opt-out

fig9.3 (federation):
- Update Peer/deliver message payload to carry broadcastMentions field (parallel to existing mentions handling)
- Document delivery-time resolution at the receiving server
- Spec receiver-side handling when send-time set differs from receiver's delivery-time set (use receiver's view; do not trust sender's id list for authorization purposes)

fig9.4 (push draft):
- Replace hasMentionAll with mentionScopes: String[] (per D6)
- Update server-side computation rule to cover both array path and rich-body span path for broadcast scopes (parallel to my existing f86f4f4 fix for hasMention)
- Update mentionUrgency trigger condition
- Update example payload to demonstrate at least one broadcast scope

Files in scope: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md (main), draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md, draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00.md. Implementer guides update naturally from those.

6gzj.4 resolved as part of M2 \u2014 closing in parallel.
